verdictOnCurrentFilms: Honestly: these are slideshows with subtitles, not films with typography. (1) No exhibit identity at all. Ford has no Anton and no #ff4b1f, Douglass has no Abril Fatface or wood-type, Persia has no Cormorant and no script. All three share one default Georgia-class serif in a rounded translucent box, so a Ford film and a Persia film are the same film. (2) Colour is accidental: every frame is backed by a blown-up blur of the photograph itself, so the Douglass title page turns the whole screen mustard, the engraving turns grey, the daguerreotype orange, and Persia's lapis never appears (it is muddy gold-brown). The palette is a side effect of whatever image is on screen, not a decision. (3) Captions are paragraphs, not captions: 3-5 lines, about 25 words, parked for the full 9 s, so nothing is timed to the voice and the reader finishes in 4 s and then stares. The box also clips the bottom of the plate (Douglass daguerreotype, Ford Highland Park line, Persia seal) in at least six frames. (4) Provenance is a ~8px grey credit in the top-right corner; the word Reconstruction is the single most important honesty label and it is the smallest thing on screen. (5) Dead and duplicate frames: Douglass frame 3 is a mid-fade ghost, Ford 2/3, Douglass 5/6 and Persia 4/5 are identical, meaning 9 s holds with no authored motion. (6) Persia shows a Syriac gospel and a Chinese stele and then types neither script. (7) The plates sit at about 65 percent of frame width inside dead blur, postage-stamp scale. What is right: the real photographs are primary and ungraded, the Highland Park line photo is excellent, faceless paintings (Ford boy at the bench, Quadricycle from behind) are the honest ones, and no word is typed faster than it can be read. Keep that restraint; replace everything else.
concept: THE LINE THAT SETS THE TYPE. One motion engine for the family: all type is driven by the narration's word-timing file, so every word, number and name enters on the voice and the film is literally typeset by the narrator. Each exhibit's metaphor is its motion grammar, not a skin: Ford = stencil stamps slammed onto iron on the downbeat of a number; Douglass = type set into a composing stick sort by sort, then pulled as a handbill proof; Persia = a lapis road line that travels left to right and carries the script, slow; Partition = a single madder line that is drawn, and then divides the frame. Three constants in every film so it reads as one family: (a) the Provenance Slate, a fixed bottom-left chip, ARCHIVE in plain ink or RECONSTRUCTION in a tracked-caps box, present on every plate for its full duration, 28px, never dimmer than 4.5:1; (b) the Room Hairline, a 2px rule across the bottom edge that doubles as progress and carries 'Room 3 of 9' so the film matches the exhibit's plan strip; (c) the Plate Rule: the archive photograph is ungraded, uncropped to its real edges, at least 60 percent of frame height, and no type ever crosses a face or the photograph's subject. Type lives in the margin column, never on the evidence.
titleSequence: 7.5 s, identical structure across the four films, exhibit-specific engine. 0.0-0.4 s: iron/ink ground in the exhibit's own ground colour (iron, iron-gall brown-black, midnight, soot), silence, room tone only. 0.4-2.6 s: ONE real archive plate arrives at full contrast (Douglass daguerreotype, Highland Park line, the Xi'an stele rubbing, a real 1947 refugee-column photograph subject to the gate), no grade, 2 percent push over the whole film opening. 2.6-5.4 s: the exhibit title is set by its engine in the margin column, never over the face: Douglass sets sort by sort ('FREDERICK / DOUGLASS' in Abril Fatface, 18-frame stick-fill, final letter lands on narration word one); Ford stamps 'HENRY FORD / & DETROIT' in Anton, two thuds 8 frames apart, #ff4b1f; Persia draws the lapis road line then sets 'THE CHURCH OF THE EAST' in Cormorant Garamond with the Syriac title large and faded behind; Partition draws the madder line and the title appears in four scripts stacked, Urdu / Hindi / Punjabi / English, all at equal weight and equal tracking. 5.4-7.5 s: a one-line slate in the sans, 'A Plajah Dossier film . 3 min 40 s . captions on', the Room hairline draws in, a content-note chip appears where relevant (Partition: 'Contains accounts of violence; read the transcript first'), then the narration begins on the next bar. No logo animation, no light leak, no lens flare.
typography: 1080p reference, tokens in px so they scale. Voice: narrator captions in Source Serif 4 Text 600 at 40px/52px, sentence case, 2 lines max, 38 characters per line. System voice (provenance, room, credit, years) in Inter Tight 500 at 26-28px, tabular figures, +40 tracking; RECONSTRUCTION is the only tracked caps at +180. Display per exhibit: FORD Anton 168-240px caps, line-height 0.92, #ff4b1f on iron #14110f, numerals in Anton Roman, stencil-cut mask on the counter and a 2px registration mark; parts-bin tag chips (rectangle 3px radius) carry credits. DOUGLASS Abril Fatface 120-200px mixed case on iron-gall #1b1511, gold #d9b36a, with a wood-type slab (Alfa Slab One / Rozha One as the licensed proxy for Clarendon-class) for single words like WRITTEN BY HIMSELF, set as a handbill stack: three sizes, ragged centre axis, rule above and below; ink squash simulated with a 0.6px displacement and a 2 percent random baseline wobble per sort. PERSIA Cormorant Garamond 500 italic for titles at 110-150px, lapis #4f7cff on midnight #0a1030; real Estrangela Syriac (Noto Sans Syriac Eastern / Serto-free, Church of the East Madnhaya form) and Noto Serif SC for the stele characters, set at 480-720px, 10-14 percent opacity, behind the margin column, never behind a plate, and also set readable at 64px beside the English where a name is spoken. PARTITION Fraunces 600 (SOFT 50, WONK 0) 130-190px on soot #181513 with madder #e8553d; Urdu in Noto Nastaliq Urdu with line-height 2.0 (the face needs it), Hindi in Noto Serif Devanagari, Punjabi in Noto Serif Gurmukhi, each at the same optical size as the Latin, order stable across the film; every non-Latin line proofed by a named native reader before render. Never track lowercase, never fake bold a script, never set Nastaliq in a Latin box.
captionsAndLowerThirds: Kill the translucent box entirely. Layout reserves a caption band so nothing overlaps: plate on a fixed 2/3 field (left), margin column 1/3 (right) holds caption, credit, year; on portrait plates the plate is full height 78 percent and caption sits below at 40px. Captions are phrase-chunked from the forced-alignment file: one chunk per spoken clause, max 2 lines, 38 chars per line, ~14 characters per second ceiling; chunk enters on the first word's onset minus 2 frames, exits at last word plus 6 frames, no fade longer than 4 frames, and the current word gets a 100 percent / others 70 percent luminance step (no karaoke bounce). Names, dates and numbers in the narration are the stressed words: they set in the exhibit's display face inline at 1.25x, in the exhibit's accent colour (e.g. 1913, 93 minutes, 781, 17 August 1947). Lower-third is one structure: a 2px accent rule 48px long, then a name or place in display face 56px, then role/date in Inter Tight 28px; it holds 3 s minimum and appears at most once per two minutes. Provenance Slate always on: 'ARCHIVE . Samuel J. Miller, about 1847-52 . Public domain' at 24px minimum, two lines, bottom-left under the plate; for paintings the slate swaps to a RECONSTRUCTION tag plus the one-line note ('Imagined; the line itself is documented in the photograph at 2:14'). Sidecar SRT and VTT in the same chunking so captions-off still has the same structure.
transitions: 1) HARD ON THE GAP (the default, about 70 percent of cuts): straight cut placed in the nearest narration silence of 120 ms or more; no effect; used between plates in the same beat. Timed: cut frame = silence start + 3 frames. 2) SLUG STAMP (Ford chapter changes, 3-4 per film): a #ff4b1f stencil bar 160px tall slams across in 6 frames, holds 4, is struck out in 6 revealing the new plate; lands on the spoken year; paired with a single dry steel tap. 3) FORME LOCK (Douglass chapter changes): the next plate and its handbill title are 'locked up' like a forme: four iron frame rules close inward over 10 frames, hold 6, open; the title sorts set in 18 frames after. 4) MILESTONE ROAD (Persia): the lapis road line sweeping L-R 24 frames at ease-in-out carries the next plate in on its edge while the faded Syriac/Chinese script parallax-slides at 0.3x; used only when the story moves place (Ctesiphon to Seleucia to Chang'an). 5) MADDER RULE (Partition): a 4px madder line is drawn top to bottom in 18 frames and the frame on either side of it is a different place; the left half holds the old plate, the right half is the new; used ONLY for place changes and for the moment the line is drawn, so it never becomes a style. 6) DIP TO GROUND (12 frames, to the exhibit's own ground colour, not black or white): time passing inside one subject only (Douglass boyhood to escape). 7) SILENCE FRAME (hold card, 2 s, no score, caption only, plate or ground): immediately before any distressing or contested passage (Partition's violence, Persia's martyrdom, Douglass's whipping account); it is the film's gate, shown with the content-note chip. 8) SCALE MATCH (rare, 1 per film): a real printed detail (title page rule, assembly-line gear, stele seal) is pushed to fill the frame in 20 frames and becomes the next section's title ground; match on shape, not on glow. No cross-dissolves between plates, no whip pans, no glitches, no light leaks, no zoom-blur.
motionGraphics: Everything is data-honest and sourced in the script; if a number is not in the narration or a cited source it does not animate. FORD: (a) CHASSIS CLOCK: two horizontal Anton bars on iron, 12 h 30 min (750 min) in grey drawn over 40 frames, then 93 min in #ff4b1f drawn in 8 frames, numeral counts with ratchet ticks at the same pace as the narration says the figures, then the 93 holds 2 s. (b) MODEL T COUNTER: parts-bin tag with a 7-digit flip counter reaching ~15,000,000 over the sentence, ending on a stencilled 'ABOUT'; the word estimated stays. (c) NAMED-WORKER ROLL: the real photographs of line workers get a stencil tag with the name only where the record names them. DOUGLASS: (a) HANDBILL TIMELINE: 1818 (about) / 1838 / 1845 set as wood-type with 'ABOUT' on the first, the real North Star masthead and the real Narrative title page shown as plates; (b) TITLE PAGE CALL-OUT: a 2px gold underline draws under the actual words WRITTEN BY HIMSELF on the real 1845 title page as the narration says it, then a 140 percent crop-in of the page, untouched pixels, no grade; (c) COMPOSING STICK: the pull-quote, if used, is set in the stick one word per spoken word with the line-height drawn by a gold rule. PERSIA: (a) THE ROAD MAP: a vector map from Natural Earth/GeoNames-sourced geometry, Ctesiphon to Seleucia to Chang'an, lapis line drawing at 42 px/s, each stop labelled in English plus real Syriac or Chinese at the same size, dated; routes drawn as dashed (traditional, uncertain) vs solid (documented) so the line itself expresses evidence strength; (b) THE STELE: 781 and 635 numerals set in Cormorant with the actual stele characters at 540px 12 percent behind, the Chinese line then pulled forward and translated by a caption, credited. PARTITION: (a) THE LINE: a map built from Radcliffe-line geometry (public boundary data), the madder line drawn from the Punjab north to south over 6 s as the narrator reads; places named in Urdu / Hindi / Punjabi / English; (b) THE RANGE BAR: displacement and deaths shown as ranges not single numbers (estimates differ widely), a bar with soft ends and the words 'estimates differ' in the sans; no body-count tickers, no rolling totals, no red flash; (c) DATE STACK: 14 August / 15 August / 17 August 1947 set as three stacked Fraunces lines, the madder underline moves between them. Static infographics render as real vector, not raster, so they stay sharp on TV.

perExhibit.douglass: Handbill and composing stick. Ground iron-gall #1b1511, gold #d9b36a, Abril Fatface display, slab for single shouted words. Delete the mustard blur fill; plates sit on a flat ground with a 1px gold rule, the daguerreotype keeps its real oval and brass edge. Motion = type sets sort by sort (first letter drops 2 frames earlier than the narration word, last lands on it); chapter change = Forme Lock. The hero moments are real documents: the Narrative title page call-out and the North Star masthead. Faceless Baltimore/boyhood paintings carry the RECONSTRUCTION slate; the faced 'lectern' and 'study' paintings are cut and replaced by real engravings/photographs. Silence frame before the account of violence. Tone: calm authority, no fanfare.
perExhibit.ford: Parts-bin and stencil. Ground iron #14110f, signal red-orange #ff4b1f only for stencilled numerals and tags; Anton caps, stencil mask, registration marks, perforated time-card edge on the room hairline. Motion = stamp on the downbeat of numbers, ratchet counters, hard cuts on narration gaps with Slug Stamp on chapter moves. Hero moments: CHASSIS CLOCK (750 to 93 minutes) over the real Highland Park line photograph, and the Model T counter. The painted Ford portrait with the pleased face is out; Ford is a photograph or back-turned. The Beliefs and Morals section gets the same stamp grammar, same type size, no theatrical light, no music swell: a Silence Frame, then the printed Dearborn Independent pages as plates with the dated masthead. Pride earned by real photographs; honesty set in the same Anton as the Rouge.
perExhibit.persia: The road. Ground midnight #0a1030, lapis #4f7cff, Cormorant Garamond italic; real Syriac and Chinese characters 500-700px, 10-14 percent, as slow-drifting ground (0.3x parallax), and readable at 64px whenever a name is spoken. Replace muddy gold with lapis and parchment. Motion = very slow: 24-frame Milestone Road, a lapis line that is the film's spine across the bottom (it is the room hairline here). Hero moment: THE ROAD MAP with solid vs dashed segments for documented vs traditional. Seal and stele plates shown at full size with their real edges; the British Museum seal credit set properly. Silence Frame before the martyrdom passage and the word 'historians debate' set as a held line. Persian church history is not Gothic romance: no lamp-lit spotlight on any plate.
perExhibit.partition: The map line. Ground soot #181513, madder #e8553d, Fraunces, four-script titles with native proofing. Motion = the line: drawn, never animated decoratively; Madder Rule only for place changes. Hero moments: THE LINE map and THE RANGE BAR (ranges, never single totals). Real photographs of refugee columns only after a Silence Frame and content-note chip, shown full-size and ungraded, no push-in and no caption over them, narrator caption below. Reconstructions limited to empty places (a station platform, a signed map table), no faces. Every title and place name proofed by named Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi readers; if proof is not in hand the title ships in English with the scripts omitted rather than wrong.

soundTies: Everything is keyed to the narration's forced-alignment JSON (word start/end, ms). Build a beat map per film: onsets of clauses, stressed tokens (names, numbers, dates), and gaps of 120 ms or more. Rules: (1) text enters 2 frames before its word's onset (the eye leads the ear by about 40 ms) and never earlier than 6 frames; (2) a number counter lands on the spoken digit, not the sentence start; (3) cuts and transitions snap to the nearest gap; a transition may not start inside a spoken word; (4) display type holds at least 12 frames and a title line at least 1.2 s; nothing outruns about 14 characters per second; (5) score is sparse, 60-72 BPM or beatless, ducked 10 dB under voice, loudness -16 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP; score hits sit on chapter transitions only; (6) sound design is specific to the metaphor and kept 20 dB under the voice: Ford = dry steel tap on the stamp, ratchet ticks for counters; Douglass = soft letterpress thud on the forme lock, type sorts as a faint click at the pace of setting; Persia = a single plucked string on the road line start, otherwise room tone; Partition = no impact sounds at all, only a held low drone and room tone; (7) Silence Frames are literally silent for 2 s (room tone off), which is the only place the music is cut. Reuse the platform's TTS timing endpoint for the Aria narration; for human narration run word-level alignment and hand-correct names.
productionMethod: 1) ENGINE: one HTML page per film with a pure function render(t) that sets all state from a timeline JSON (word timings, plate list, transition list, graphics list); Playwright steps t by 1/30 s, screenshots 1920x1080 PNG (deterministic, no wall-clock), real fonts via @font-face with local files so shaping (HarfBuzz) is correct for Syriac, Nastaliq, Devanagari, Gurmukhi. Plain CSS/SVG for type, rules, bars, counters and maps (d3-geo over Natural Earth); canvas or WebGL ONLY for ink-squash and paper displacement on the type layer, never on photographs. 2) ENCODE: ffmpeg x264 CRF 16, yuv420p, bt709, 30 fps, +faststart; audio mux from the narration + score stems, loudnorm to -16 LUFS; SRT/VTT sidecars from the same chunker; render per-chapter segments in parallel (4 workers) then concat with crossfade-free joins. 3) SHARED KIT in the platform: tokens file (colours, type scale, easing, durations), the Provenance Slate and Room Hairline components, the beat-map builder, and the four per-exhibit engines as CSS/JS modules, so a fifth exhibit is a config. 4) LOTTIE/dotLottie: only for small reusable bits that must also live in the app UI (stamp slam, tick, the ARCHIVE/RECONSTRUCTION chip flip), not for title sequences. 5) FABULA/TELA: use Fabula's FX preview and editable tracks for the interactive Dossier-embedded version and for the narrator/caption timing pass, and Tela for the static title-card and still-slate layouts that match the exhibit's Room template; export JSON between Tela and the engine so type specs are single-sourced. 6) MAGNIFIC: spend credits only on faceless texture plates (iron, handbill paper, lime plaster, soot) and on replacing the faced paintings with faceless or back-turned reconstructions; NO generative video on people or archival material, no animating Douglass. 7) PILLOW + QA: contact sheets, automated overlap/contrast check (caption box vs plate bbox, 4.5:1 minimum), frame-diff to detect dead or duplicate holds, per-frame text-in-safe-area test; manual native-reader sign-off for every non-Latin string; honesty checklist (every plate has a slate, every number sourced) as a gate before encode.
risk: Type-first films give up the cheap drama of full-screen painted frames, so a viewer expecting a trailer may call them austere, and the engine is a real build (about four films of custom timelines plus a shared kit); the mitigation is the shared kit and a data-driven timeline. Technical risk: non-Latin shaping and Nastaliq vertical metrics in Chromium and font licences (all SIL OFL Noto/Google fonts, Anton, Abril Fatface, Cormorant, Fraunces are OFL), and the real risk of a wrong or misspelled script word; we ship English-only before we ship unproofed script. Ethical risk: kinetic type on the Beliefs and Partition material can slide into spectacle; the Silence Frame and the identical-grammar rule are the defence, and any single moment where a transition is flashy next to distress should be cut. A slow 2 percent push on a photograph could read as grading or manipulation: capped at 3 percent, linear, disclosed on the slate as 'camera move added', never on a distressing plate. Distressing images stay gated behind the content-note chip, never in thumbnails or title plates without a click-through.

arguesWith.why: GENERATIVE will want to spend the Magnific credits on animating the reconstructions into moving generative video and on procedural, AI-generated title backgrounds. I say no for these films: any moving painted human is an invented face in motion, honesty over polish rules it out, and generated B-roll turns the exhibit identity into the same tea-brown that is already the generic problem. The motion is in the type, the line, the stamp and the real photograph held still; I will give GENERATIVE texture plates and faceless place reconstructions, and the right to try procedural paper and ink as the transition substrate, but not people and not archive.
